idiom_name: token struct with a private (or pub(in path)) field; module-restricted construction, and pub(in ...) on the operation when the grantee is a module
implementation_notes: Rust has no friend-to-type and no per-collaborator grant: visibility is module-based, and construction rights follow the visibility of a struct's fields. A public token struct with a private field can be named everywhere but built only inside its module - the compiler reports 'cannot initialise a tuple struct which contains private fields' (E0423) elsewhere - while pub(in crate::owner) on the field extends construction to exactly that module's subtree and pub(crate) widens it to the crate. The restricted method then takes the token as a parameter, and any holder may call it, which is the delegation mechanism. When the grantee is a module rather than a type, skip the token: a plain pub(in crate::grantee) fn on the operation expresses the same grant without ceremony.
pitfalls: Visibility is module-based, never type-based: pub(in crate::subtree) on the token field grants every item in that subtree, not just the collaborator you had in mind.
A token with a public field - or a unit struct such as 'pub struct Key;' - is forgeable; the field must be private.
Deriving Clone or Copy makes the grant transitive by accident; derive nothing on the token and pass it by value only where you intend it.
